chunks: Farewell to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his minbar.

When you wish to leave al-Madinah, go to the place of the head of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and greet him. Then go to the minbar and send blessings there upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله as much as you are able, and supplicate for yourself with whatever you wish concerning religion and worldly life. Then return to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and place your left shoulder against the grave, near the pillar that is before the rear pillar at the head of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Then perform six rak'ahs or eight rak'ahs, and recite al-Hamd and a surah in every rak'ah, and perform qunut in every two rak'ahs.

When you have finished them, face the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and say, bidding him farewell, upon him السلام: "May Allah send blessings upon you; peace be upon you. May Allah not make this my final greeting to you. O Allah, do not make this the last عهد of visiting the grave of Your Prophet, Your blessings be upon him and his family. And if You cause me to die before that, then I testify in my death to what I testify in my life: that there is no god but You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger."

key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madinah, the city from which the visitor departs
key_terms.الْمِنْبَرَ: the pulpit of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.تَوْدِيعُ: farewell-taking at the time of departure
key_terms.رَسُولُكَ: Your Messenger, referring to Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَاقْنُتْ: perform qunut, the supplicatory invocation in prayer

ai.seo_question: How does one bid farewell to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم according to Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage describes the etiquette of bidding farewell to the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in al-Madinah. It includes prescribed acts of salutation, salat, du'a, and a farewell formula expressing hope to return and affirming tawhid and the risalah of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
